original_question: What is the local deformation theory of G2-instantons on asymptotically conical G2-manifolds? More specifically, can one understand the local geometry of their moduli space, prove a uniqueness result for the basic G2-instanton on R^7 with gauge group G2, decide whether deformations of symmetric G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds must preserve the same symmetries, and determine the properties of the natural projection from the moduli space of G2-instantons to the moduli space of nearly Kahler instantons, including whether that projection is surjective?
target_in_paper: Section §3.3, Open problems (c), with essential setup from §3 and closely related asymptotic-limit context from Open problems (b).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies that the paper is asking for the local geometry of the moduli space of G2-instantons on asymptotically conical (AC) G2-manifolds, i.e. their local deformation theory, and it accurately reproduces the three concrete subquestions listed by the authors: uniqueness of the basic G2-instanton on R^7 with gauge group G2, whether deformations of symmetric G2-instantons remain symmetric, and the behavior of the natural map to the moduli space of nearly Kähler instantons, including possible surjectivity.
missing_details: The paper’s question is local near a fixed AC G2-instanton and its gauge-equivalence class; it is not asking for a full global classification of all G2-instantons on all AC G2-manifolds.
To be fully stand-alone, one should specify the AC hypothesis: X^7 is a complete noncompact torsion-free G2-manifold with one end asymptotic to the cone R^+ x M over a nearly Kähler 6-manifold M.
The relevant moduli spaces should be understood for a fixed principal bundle P -> X (and fixed structure group G) and taken modulo gauge transformations.

The projection to the nearly Kähler moduli space is the asymptotic-limit map, so one should state the decay hypothesis used in the surrounding context: the G2-instanton has pointwise decaying curvature at infinity and admits a limit connection on the link M.

The target of that projection should be identified precisely: the moduli space of pseudo-Hermitian–Yang–Mills (nearly Kähler) connections a on M satisfying F_a wedge omega^2 = 0 and F_a wedge gamma_2 = 0.

The symmetry question is posed in the paper in the cohomogeneity-1 setting: if a G2-instanton is constructed using the manifold’s symmetry, must nearby deformations preserve that same symmetry so that at least one component of the moduli space remains describable by the survey’s symmetric ODE methods?
The uniqueness subproblem concerns the specific "basic" G2-instanton on R^7 cited from [GN95], with gauge group G2.

No algebraic ambient field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the hidden assumptions are geometric: fixed bundle, gauge quotient, AC asymptotic model, decay at infinity, and symmetry class.
refined_question: Let (X^7, phi) be an asymptotically conical G2-manifold, i.e. a complete noncompact torsion-free G2-manifold with one end asymptotic to the cone R^+ x M over a nearly Kähler 6-manifold (M, omega, gamma_2). Fix a principal G-bundle P -> X and a G2-instanton A on P whose curvature decays pointwise at infinity, so that A has an asymptotic limit a on M satisfying F_a wedge omega^2 = 0 and F_a wedge gamma_2 = 0. What is the local deformation theory of A, equivalently the local geometry of the moduli space of G2-instantons on X modulo gauge near [A]? In particular, can one prove uniqueness of the basic G2-instanton on R^7 with gauge group G2, determine whether deformations of symmetric G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds must preserve the same symmetries (so that at least one cohomogeneity-1 component of the moduli space is still accessible by the symmetric methods used in the survey), and analyze the asymptotic-limit projection from the local moduli space of G2-instantons to the moduli space of nearly Kähler instantons on M, including whether this map is surjective?
equivalent_formulation: Understand the local geometry of the moduli space of G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds; equivalently, develop the deformation theory of such G2-instantons.
justification: The nearest official target is not a theorem or conjecture but Open problems §3.3(c), which asks exactly for the local geometry of the moduli space of G2-instantons on AC G2-manifolds and then spells out the same three follow-up questions your draft lists. To make the question fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the AC setup from the start of §3 and the asymptotic-limit discussion from §3 and Open problems (b): an AC G2-manifold is asymptotic to a cone over a nearly Kähler link, and G2-instantons with pointwise decaying curvature have nearly Kähler instanton limits there. The symmetry subquestion is motivated by the cohomogeneity-1 moduli-space descriptions developed earlier in §3.2, especially the invariant Bryant–Salamon examples, while the nearly Kähler projection question is motivated by the fact that those examples share a canonical nearly Kähler limit at infinity.
